title: Samosa

seo.title: Authentic Pakistani Samosa Recipe: Easy Homemade Guide
seo.metaDescription: Learn how to make the best authentic Pakistani Samosa recipe at home! This easy step-by-step guide ensures crispy, flavorful samosas perfect for any occasion.
h2Headings: Pro Tips for the Best Results
seo.imageAlt: Crispy golden authentic Pakistani Samosa with spicy potato filling, served with mint chutney.
seo.imageCaption: Enjoy these perfectly golden, crispy authentic Pakistani Samosas – a beloved Pakistani appetizer for any gathering!

description: Samosas are an iconic Pakistani street food and a beloved snack, featuring a crispy, golden-fried pastry shell. They are traditionally filled with a delicious blend of spiced potatoes, peas, and sometimes minced meat, offering a burst of savory flavors with every bite. Perfect for tea time or festive occasions, these triangular delights are a true culinary masterpiece.

ingredients.notes: for dough, plus to taste for filling

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon salt, and carom seeds. Add 1/4 cup vegetable oil and mix with your fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs. Gradually add water, a little at a time, kneading until a firm, smooth dough forms. Cover the dough with a damp cloth and let it rest for at least 15 minutes.

instructions.title: Cook the Filling Base
instructions.text: While the dough rests, prepare the filling. Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté until translucent, about 3-4 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste, finely chopped green chilies, and cumin seeds. Cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Combine Filling Ingredients
instructions.text: Add coriander powder, red chili powder, turmeric powder, and garam masala to the pan. Sauté for 30 seconds to cook the spices. Then, add the boiled and mashed potatoes along with the green peas. Mix well, ensuring the spices are evenly distributed throughout the potato mixture. Season with salt to taste. Remove from heat, stir in the fresh cilantro and chaat masala, and let the filling cool completely.

instructions.title: Shape the Samosas
instructions.text: Divide the rested dough into equal small balls. Roll each ball into an oval shape, about 6-7 inches long. Cut each oval in half to create two semi-circles. Take one semi-circle, moisten the straight edge with a little water, and fold it into a cone shape, pressing the seam firmly. Fill the cone with 2-3 tablespoons of the cooled potato mixture. Moisten the open edges of the cone with water and seal them to form a triangular samosa, ensuring no gaps.

instructions.title: Heat the Frying Oil
instructions.text: In a deep pan or wok, heat enough vegetable oil for deep frying over medium-low heat. It is crucial that the oil is not too hot; a temperature of around 160-170°C (325-340°F) is ideal for perfectly crispy samosas. Test the oil by dropping a small piece of dough; it should sizzle gently and slowly rise to the surface.

instructions.title: Fry the Samosas
instructions.text: Carefully place 3-4 samosas into the hot oil, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Fry the samosas on medium-low heat, turning them occasionally, until they turn a beautiful golden brown and are crispy on all sides. This slow frying process ensures that the pastry cooks thoroughly and becomes flaky.

instructions.title: Drain and Serve
instructions.text: Once golden brown and crispy, remove the fried samosas from the oil using a slotted spoon. Place them on a plate lined with paper towels to drain any excess oil. Serve the hot, crispy Pakistani Samosas immediately with fresh mint chutney, tamarind chutney, or ketchup for a truly delightful appetizer.

tips: For truly crispy samosas, fry them on medium-low heat. This allows the pastry to cook through and become golden without burning.
Add a pinch of dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi) to the potato filling for an extra layer of authentic Pakistani flavor.
Samosas are best served hot immediately after frying. You can freeze un-fried samosas for up to a month; just fry them directly from frozen.
